task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: The Global Weather Repository reveals stark regional temperature disparities. By average temperature, Middle Eastern cities dominate: Ar Riyadh leads at 45.0°C, followed by Kuwait at 44.4°C. However, single hottest measurements tell a different story—Suva reaches an extreme 79.3°C, dwarfing the second-hottest reading of 49.2°C in Kuwait City. At the country level, Saudi Arabien averages 45.0°C, while Fiji Islands records the highest single measurement at 79.3°C. A striking pattern emerges: Gulf and Middle Eastern nations (Qatar, UAE, Oman) cluster across multiple rankings, indicating sustained heat rather than isolated peaks. Djibouti appears in both city and country maximum lists at 47.1°C, reinforcing regional consistency in extreme heat.

At the country level, Saudi Arabia averages 45.0°C, while Fiji Islands records the highest single measurement at 79.3°C.
